_comment: Portable safety FLOOR as data (ADR-0001 trust model + ADR-0008 egress). Reader: harness/claude-code/guard.py. Proven by harness/claude-code/golden_test.py. Eval order: hard_deny -> slack_send -> drive_write -> fs_write -> bash_deny -> default allow. Fail mode closed (parse error => deny). v2 INTENTIONALLY diverges from the legacy nova-guard: (a) Amp is a first-party coder with broad local authority, so fs_write allow_roots is the whole home tree + /tmp (legacy was 4 narrow roots); (b) in exchange, secret material is hard-denied across BOTH the write tools AND bash (legacy left bash writes/reads ungated) — closing the bash bypass. The outward gates (slack, drive) are unchanged.
_comment_v3: v3 (ADR-0015, 2026-07-16): REVERSIBLE inbox hygiene is no longer hard-denied — archive_email, trash_email (Gmail's recoverable 30-day bin), batch_update_emails, and gmail update_email (label mods) now fall through to default_allow. This RESTORES ADR-0001's original posture ('archive noise: allowed', 'label/move reversible: allowed') that the v2 clamp over-tightened. Safety for these moved UP the stack: a deterministic guardrail layer + an independent review agent + batch approval + a full undo log (apps/amp-tasks/inbox-sweep.js, review-agent.js). The floor's job here narrows to its honest core: PERMANENT destruction stays hard-denied — every delete_* (incl. delete_email, delete_draft, delete_label) and the bare __delete tool remain blocked. Nothing the sweeper does is irreversible.

slack_send._comment: Preserves Python precedence: match if (slack_send_message) OR (send_message AND 'slack' substring). All regex re.I. Once matched, ALWAYS exits (allow or deny) - never falls through.
slack_send._channel_id_whitelist_note: amp-brief=C0AMPBRIEF, amp-alerts=C0AMPALERT, amp-brief-staging=C0AMPSTG (created 2026-06-25). Old nova-brief=C0LEGACY01 archived same day; nova-alerts and nova-brief-staging never existed as real channels.

drive_write._comment: If matched AND 'drive' substring, ALWAYS allow (non-share write). Sharing changes are caught earlier by hard_deny add_file_sharing_preference.

fs_write._comment: Eval: empty target => allow. Else if target matches sensitive_path_patterns => DENY (secrets, any root). Else if target under no allow_root => DENY. Else allow. allow_roots is broad (home + tmp) by design; secrets are the real gate.

bash_deny._sensitive_comment: If the command references a sensitive_path AND shows read or write intent toward it, deny. Closes the bash bypass that left ~/.ssh etc. ungated. Read-intent is re.I.
bash_deny.sensitive_reason: bash access to secret material is blocked (ADR-0001; no secrets into GenAI)
